Condensed structural formula: (CH₃)₃CH.
The melting and boiling points generally increase as the size and molecular mass of the alkanes increase.
Alkanes are relatively unreactive because they have strong C—C and C—H single bonds and no reactive functional group.
n-Butane has a higher boiling point than iso-butane because its unbranched molecules have a larger surface area for intermolecular attraction.

Choose the longest continuous carbon chain as the parent chain; its carbon count gives the root name, and the suffix -ane identifies an alkane. Number the chain from the end nearest a branch, then give each branch its name and position number. Use prefixes such as di- or tri- for repeated branches.
